title: Add burn-rate alert templates + recommended Private SLOs/window pairs
author: Allison Grant
release_notes:
- Adds reusable burn-rate helper templates (multi-window, multi-burn) used by Private observability min pack PrometheusRule bundles.
- Documents recommended default SLOs and alert window pairs for Private installs (VPC/on-prem).
body:
Context: The Private observability minimum pack is standardizing on burn-rate paging for API availability/latency and a small set of pipeline health alerts. In practice we were copy/pasting slightly different burn-rate expressions across repos (observability-pack, helm charts) and drifting on window pairs + severity mapping. This PR adds reusable templates/helpers in slo-toolkit and a concise doc of Redwood-recommended SLOs + alert window pairs for Private, so downstream repos can generate consistent PrometheusRule groups.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a small library for generating multi-window burn-rate alerts ("fast" + "slow" pair) with consistent labels/annotations and runbook URL formatting.
- Adds helpers for common SLI styles used in Private pack: request success rate (5xx + explicit error_code), request latency (histogram-based), and "missing metrics" (absence) safeguards.
- Documents recommended defaults for Private (initial GA): SLO targets, evaluation windows, burn thresholds, and severity mapping (page vs ticket) aligned with SRE paging policy.
- Adds unit-style validation to ensure produced rules parse and contain required labels (service, slo, severity, team) to support routing and auditability.

Why in slo-toolkit: We want a single source-of-truth for burn-rate math + window pairing so that (a) thresholds are explainable and (b) fixes (like rate()/increase() pitfalls and label joins) can be shipped once.

Recommended defaults included in docs (summary):
- Gateway/API availability SLO: 99.9% monthly; burn alert pair: 5m/1h at 14x + 30m/6h at 6x (page), and 2h/1d at 3x (ticket).
- Gateway/API latency SLO (p95): 99% of requests under per-route target; burn pair: 5m/1h at 8x + 30m/6h at 4x (page) with guidance to tune per deployment.
- Control plane critical endpoints availability SLO: 99.9% monthly; use only the slow pair for page by default to reduce noise in smaller installs.

Notes / constraints:
- Templates assume Prometheus-compatible query semantics and PrometheusRule CRD consumers; they do not assume Thanos/Ruler or a managed backend.
- Labels are intentionally low-cardinality and avoid tenant/model labels by default; downstream rules can add scoping via recording rules if needed.
- For Private on-prem, we keep evaluation windows conservative to avoid paging on short-lived scrape gaps; docs include a section on scrape interval dependencies.

Follow-ups:
- observability-pack will switch to importing these templates for the Private min pack rule bundle (tracked in ENG-2843).
- Once rule groups are wired into redwood-private-installer, we should add an end-to-end check in the validation harness that asserts labels + annotations match this contract.

Checklist:
- [x] promtool rule validation added to CI for the rendered examples
- [x] docs added with window pair rationale + tuning guidance
- [x] severity mapping reviewed by SRE (paging policy)
- [x] annotations include stable runbook URL + dashboard link placeholders

Testing:
- `make test` (includes jsonnet render + promtool check)
- `make render-examples` and confirm output matches docs

References:
- Linear: ENG-2843 (Private PrometheusRule bundle), ENG-2860 (noise review + tuning)
- Support context: SUP-2431 (rule load failures after upgrade; this PR adds stricter render/parse checks)
- Downstream PRs: observability-pack PR-322 will consume these helpers for SLO burn alerts

sli: add request success/latency helper constructors (histogram + error_code)

ci: add render + promtool validation for example rule bundles

review_conversation: Sean Gallagher (SRE) — Requested change: "Can we standardize severity labels to match paging routing (page/ticket) and ensure the annotation includes the SLO target + burn multipliers so oncall can reason quickly?"

Allison Grant (author) — Reply: "Updated labels to `severity=page|ticket` (dropping `critical|warning` mapping) and added `summary`/`description` templates to include SLO, windows, burn. Pushed commit `lint: normalize annotation keys and runbook URL builder`."

Sergio Costa — Requested change: "Downstream dashboards expect `slo` label; please make it required and documented. Also add a stable annotation key for dashboard link even if we fill it later in the pack."
Allison Grant (author) — Reply: "Added `slo` as required param in helper, enforced in render tests. Added `redwood.dashboard_uid` annotation placeholder + documented how downstream can set it."
Nadia Rahman — Comment: "Good call on avoiding tenant/model labels. Please add a short note warning about cardinality if folks try to do per-model burn alerts."
Allison Grant (author) — Reply: "Added 'Cardinality and scoping' section in docs with recommended approach (recording rules + aggregate at route/service)."
Bruno Silva — Comment: "Installer validation will check for required labels. Can we freeze the minimal set: service, team, severity, slo?"
Allison Grant (author) — Reply: "Yes—documented as required contract and enforced by example render check."
Sean Gallagher — Approval: "Looks good. Window pairs align with our Private alerting philosophy (slow pair only for small clusters). Approved."
Sergio Costa — Approval: "Approved; will reference these helpers in observability-pack rule generation."
